rows.name: Mattermost
rows.reason: Its open-source Team Edition server and web client support self-hosted team chat, with documented browser and mobile clients; enterprise-only features are unnecessary for these requirements.

rows.name: Rocket.Chat non-enterprise core
rows.reason: Rocket.Chat core offers self-hosting/web/mobile, but MIT excludes enterprise directories. Mobile-source retrieval failed; native-client licensing, advanced features/limits and broad keyboard operation remain unresolved. No extra requirements are inferred.

rows.name: Mattermost — open-source edition
rows.reason: Self-hosted open-source chat with web/Android/iOS clients. Select open-source edition; inspect version-specific licensing/features against commercial editions. Coverage of most features without a mouse unestablished.

rows.name: Element Web with a self-hosted Synapse server
rows.reason: Open-source browser client/server requires operating both. Mobile web is community-supported and defines recommendation scope; native Element X licenses uninspected. Optional broad keyboard use unverified.

rows.name: Zulip
rows.reason: Documented required-feature fit with broad optional keyboard controls and topic-based conversations. Exhaustive keyboard-only usability untested; live documentation cannot establish exact features on 2020-06-24.

rows.name: Discord
rows.reason: Official client terms restrict use/modification/redistribution, contradicting required open-source status. Component exceptions do not establish whole-client openness; no unsupported-server or self-hosting claim is needed.

rows.name: Rocket (Rust web framework)
rows.reason: Rust web framework requires implementing the requested team-chat system and interfaces. Framework open-source status does not supply an existing complete alternative; operating-scope mismatch.

rows.name: Mattermost open-source core
rows.reason: Self-hosted web/mobile chat; core/web licensing established, required native-client open-source licensing unverified. Commercial offerings remain distinct; paid features not assumed open-source. Broad keyboard operation unchecked.

rows.name: Rocket (Rust web framework)
rows.reason: Rocket is a Rust web framework for implementing applications, not a finished chat system with server, web GUI and mobile interface.

rows.name: Rocket.Chat — community/core configuration
rows.reason: Self-hosted core messaging supplies web/mobile access; exclude enterprise-only components. Repository separates MIT core/enterprise directories. Native mobile licensing, broad keyboard coverage and dated pre-cutoff release evidence unverified.

rows.name: Discord
rows.reason: Discord supplies proprietary client software for its hosted service, not the required open-source client/server pair that the user can self-host.

rows.name: The Lounge with an InspIRCd server
rows.reason: MIT web IRC client/GPLv2 server provides responsive smartphone access. Operate both; evaluate IRC/Slack feature differences. Not one packaged Slack replacement; broad keyboard coverage unverified.

rows.name: Zulip
rows.reason: Open-source self-hostable chat server/clients provide browser/mobile access and broad optional keyboard shortcuts. Topic-based workflow differs from Slack; current features/plans cannot establish June 2020 availability.

rows.name: Mattermost
rows.reason: Retain Mattermost open-source core and web/mobile clients with self-hosting. Use compatible server/mobile releases; documentation does not establish that every commercial edition or add-on is open source.
